messages:
alex_support: FYI - ACME reporting 429s on /v1/rerank starting ~11:18 PST. They say latency spiked first, then steady 429s. Pasted their failing curl + response below.

alex_support: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-ACME" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"queries":["find best match"],"candidates":[...],"top_k":5}'

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RW-Ratelimit-Limit: 120
X-RW-Ratelimit-Remaining: 0
X-RW-Ratelimit-Reset: 18

{"error":"quota_exceeded","message":"Rerank capacity exceeded for API key","retry_after":18}```

maria_engineer: Thanks. Two immediate asks: (1) full request payload sizes (tokens per candidate + #candidates) and (2) concurrent clients/threads hitting their key. Rerank multiplies token work by #candidates so quota consumption can be much higher than plain generate.

alex_support: They've sent the full payload: batch of 50 candidates, avg candidate ~120 tokens, top_k 5. Concurrency ~8 parallel connections from their service. They previously ran this weekly, recently switched to real-time scoring every user action.

kevin_sre: That matches a quota-bomb: 50 candidates * 120 tokens * 8 concurrency = ~48k token-score operations per second-ish (rough calc). Our per-key QPS and token quotas can hit hard with rerank. Also see remaining=0 header — definitely rate-limited.

maria_engineer: Repro tip for triage: run a reduced curl with batch_size 5 and single concurrency to compare token costs. Also check our internal meter: prod -> metrics -> rerank_tokens_by_key for their key id.

alex_support: I pulled metrics: spike at 11:16 -> sustained high usage. Linking dashboard: https://internal.redwood/metrics/keys/sk-live-ACME/rerank_tokens (shared in thread).

sam_ops_bot: auto-note: Created incident INC-2026-482 and throttling alert triggered. Recommended temporary mitigations: (a) advise customer to lower candidate batch_size to 10, (b) implement exponential backoff on 429s using retry_after, (c) request quota increase ticket via support portal.

maria_engineer: Also propose short-term server-side fallback: if rerank returns 429, fallback to lighter heuristic ranking (embedding-based cosine) on our side or their side. For long term: product should consider a rerank-specific token quota separate from general generation quota or burst credits for scoring workloads.

kevin_sre: I've temporarily bumped their soft quota on the gateway to reduce immediate errors (small cushion only). Created follow-up ticket ENG-6421 to evaluate per-route rate limits and tiered burst for rerank traffic.

alex_support: I'll communicate the immediate mitigations to ACME: reduce batch_size, add backoff, and expect fewer 429s now. Also asking them for a schedule when they'll move to lower throughput or purchase Dedicated capacity.

maria_engineer: Saved repro curl and a minimal test harness in /devx/rerank/repro/2064507890-repro.sh so we can iterate. Next steps: collector logs for that API key, confirm whether cache/prefix hits could reduce cost (they don't currently use caching), and sync with product on quota model.

kevin_sre: Marking as resolved for customer immediate impact — will keep ENG-6421 open. If ACME wants predictable throughput we should recommend Dedicated or an agreed quota bump with monitoring.

alex_support: Thanks all :thumbsup: I'll close the customer-facing loop and paste update here once ACME confirms their end changes.
